title: A Family Camping Trip
passage:
Last weekend, the Wang family planned to go camping at a lake near the mountains. On Friday night, Dad checked the weather forecast and said, "If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the trip." Luckily, the sky was clear on Saturday morning, so they packed the car and set off early.

When they arrived at the campsite, Mom reminded everyone, "You'd better put on sunscreen before we set up the tent." The tent looked complicated, but with everyone's help, it was ready in twenty minutes. Tim, the youngest, wanted to carry the heaviest cooler by himself, but it was too heavy for him to lift. His sister, Amy, who was strong enough to help, carried it together with him.

In the afternoon, they went hiking along a trail beside the lake. The guide warned that the path was too narrow for two people to walk side by side, so they walked in a single line. They were lucky enough to see a family of ducks swimming near the shore.

At night, they cooked dinner over a campfire and told stories under the stars. Dad said, "If we come back next month, we should bring a bigger tent." Everyone agreed that camping together was more fun than staying at a hotel.

Before they left on Sunday, they made sure to put out the fire completely and clean up all their trash. "If every camper takes care of nature," the park ranger told them, "this lake will stay beautiful for years." The Wang family smiled and promised to return soon.

vocab.example: They set up their tent at a campsite near the lake.
Dad checked the weather forecast before the trip.
They had to cancel the trip because of the storm.
Setting up the new tent looked complicated at first.
Tim tried to carry the heavy cooler by himself.
The mountain path was too narrow for two people to walk side by side.
They went hiking along a trail beside the lake.
The guide warned them to stay on the path.
A family of ducks was swimming near the shore.
They cooked dinner over a campfire and told stories.
The park ranger reminded campers to protect nature.
The Wang family promised to return to the lake soon.
They made sure to put out the campfire completely.

grammar: 第一條件句 (First Conditional)：If + 主詞 + 現在簡單式, 主詞 + will + 動詞原形，用來描述「未來很可能發生」的真實情況。例：If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the trip. / If every camper takes care of nature, this lake will stay beautiful.
too...to 與 enough to：too + 形容詞/副詞 + (for sb) + to V 表示「太...以致不能」；形容詞/副詞 + enough + (for sb) + to V 表示「足夠...可以」。兩者語意剛好相反。例：It was too heavy for him to lift. / She was strong enough to help him.
had better (+not) + 動詞原形：表示「最好(不要)...」，常用於建議或警告，語氣比 should 更強烈，have/has 可省略為 'd。例：You'd better put on sunscreen before we set up the tent.

reading.q: Why did Dad say they might cancel the camping trip?
opts: Because it might rain the next day
reading.ex: 文中 Dad 說 "If it rains tomorrow, we will cancel the trip."，表示若下雨就取消，故選 B。

reading.q: What problem did Tim have with the cooler?
opts: It was too heavy for him to lift alone
It was too small for the food
reading.ex: 文中提到 "it was too heavy for him to lift"，因此他需要姊姊 Amy 的幫忙，故選 A。

reading.q: Why did the family walk in a single line on the trail?
opts: Because they wanted to race each other
Because the guide told a joke
Because the path was too narrow for two people to walk side by side
reading.ex: 文中寫 "the path was too narrow for two people to walk side by side, so they walked in a single line."，故選 C。

reading.q: What did Dad suggest for their next camping trip?
reading.ex: 文中 Dad 說 "If we come back next month, we should bring a bigger tent."，故選 A。

reading.q: What did the family do before leaving the campsite on Sunday?
opts: They put out the fire completely and cleaned up their trash
They bought souvenirs from the ranger
They went swimming one more time
reading.ex: 文中寫 "they made sure to put out the fire completely and clean up all their trash."，故選 B。

grammar.q: If it ___ tomorrow, we will cancel the trip.
grammar.ex: 第一條件句中 if 子句要用現在簡單式，主詞 it 為第三人稱單數，故動詞加 s，選 B。

grammar.q: If every camper takes care of nature, this lake ___ beautiful for years.
grammar.ex: 第一條件句的主要子句要用 will + 動詞原形，表示未來的結果，故選 C。

grammar.q: The cooler was ___ heavy for Tim to lift by himself.
grammar.ex: too + 形容詞 + for sb + to V 表示「太...以致某人不能」，故選 B。

grammar.q: Amy was strong ___ to help Tim carry the cooler.
grammar.ex: 形容詞 + enough + to V 表示「足夠...可以」，enough 要放在形容詞之後，故選 C。

grammar.q: You ___ put on sunscreen before we set up the tent.
grammar.ex: had better + 動詞原形表示「最好...」，不可加 to，故選 A。

vocab.q: Choose the word that means "a piece of land used for camping."
vocab.ex: campsite 意為「露營地」，故選 A。

vocab.q: A box used to keep food and drinks cold is called a ___.
vocab.ex: cooler 指「保冷箱」，用來保持食物飲料冰涼，故選 A。

vocab.q: The mountain path was very ___, so only one person could walk at a time.
vocab.ex: narrow 意為「狹窄的」，符合句意，故選 A。

vocab.q: A person whose job is to protect a park and help visitors is called a ___.
vocab.ex: ranger 指「巡山員、公園管理員」，負責保護公園，故選 B。

vocab.q: They sat around the ___ and told stories at night.
vocab.ex: campfire 意為「營火」，符合夜晚圍坐講故事的情境，故選 A。
